**Arithmetic Coding:** Encode the significance and magnitude information using the arithmetic coder.
**Rate-Distortion Optimization (RDO):** Determine the truncation point for each code-block to maximize the rate-distortion performance.
- **Code-Block Size > 32×32×32:** Using code-blocks larger than $32 \times 32 \times 32$ (e.g., $64 \times 64 \times 32$) causes a drop in coding performance.
- **Standard JPEG 2000 Compatibility:** Volumetric code-blocks are not supported by JPEG 2000 Part 1 or Part 2.
- **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the code-block size.

- **Measured Performance:** For medical volumetric data, switching from $16 \times 16 \times 1$ to $32 \times 32 \times 1$ improves compression efficiency by about 0.7 dB or 10% in bit-rate reduction.
Switching to $64 \times 64 \times 1$ improves it by about 1 dB.
Volumetric Code-Block EBCOT is a technique developed for the compression of volumetric medical images.
It is part of the JP3D standard, which extends JPEG 2000 to support 3D data.
The method leverages the 3D wavelet transform to exploit correlations between slices, and the EBCOT algorithm to provide embedded bitstreams with rate-distortion optimization.
